rule_out_checklist.item: Has the dizziness suddenly become severe, or is it a kind of dizziness you have not had before?
rule_out_checklist.why_it_matters: A sharp change is worth describing to a doctor so they can decide whether it needs a closer look.

rule_out_checklist.item: Does light sensitivity come with new vision loss, new double vision, or a headache that is much worse than usual?
rule_out_checklist.why_it_matters: Those details help a doctor tell everyday light sensitivity apart from something they may want to check sooner.

rule_out_checklist.item: Have you noticed weakness, trouble speaking, fainting, or a recent head impact that has not been checked yet?
rule_out_checklist.why_it_matters: This is a question to raise with a doctor. This demo does not decide whether symptoms are urgent.

pathways.name: Dizziness and balance questions
pathways.summary: A roadmap for talking about dizziness: what sets it off, how balance feels day to day, and which details to bring to a GP. It does not explain the cause or promise that symptoms will change.
supported_by: Parachute Canadian Guideline on Concussion in Sport

steps.title: Describe dizziness and balance with a vestibular physiotherapist
steps.rationale: Dizziness sits in the vestibular area of this demo. This visit is for listing triggers, such as turning the head or busy places, so those notes can go to a GP.

steps.title: Add questions about neck comfort and everyday movement
steps.rationale: People with dizziness sometimes also want words for neck stiffness or how movement feels. This step collects those questions. It does not say the neck is the cause.

pathways.name: Light sensitivity and visual comfort
pathways.summary: A roadmap for talking about light sensitivity: screens, reading, and bright rooms, plus what to ask a GP. It does not test vision or prescribe treatment.

steps.title: Describe light sensitivity and visual comfort with a vision therapist
steps.rationale: Light sensitivity sits in the ocular area of this demo. This visit is for noting which lights, screens, or reading tasks are hard, so a GP can hear the pattern.

steps.title: List how light sensitivity changes daily activity
steps.rationale: A sports medicine conversation can turn those visual notes into questions about work, school, or exercise to raise with a GP. It is not a clearance to return to activity.

pathways.name: Dizziness and light sensitivity together
pathways.summary: A roadmap that keeps both symptoms in one set of notes for a GP: dizziness first, then light sensitivity, then questions about activity. The order is for the conversation, not a treatment plan.
supported_by: Ontario Neurotrauma Foundation guideline for concussion and prolonged symptoms

steps.title: Start with dizziness and balance notes
steps.rationale: The first conversation captures when dizziness shows up and what makes it stronger, using the vestibular practitioner type in this demo.

steps.title: Add light sensitivity and visual comfort notes
steps.rationale: The second conversation adds light, screen, and reading details so both symptom areas are written down before a GP visit.

steps.title: Gather activity questions for a GP
steps.rationale: The last conversation turns the dizziness and light notes into questions about daily activity. Those questions are for a GP. This step does not promise a timeline or an outcome.

disclaimer: These pathways are a navigation roadmap to take to a GP. They are not a diagnosis, a prescription, or medical advice, and they do not promise any outcome.
